windows: If the love still isn’t coming, you can at least stop judging your little one.

If you have advice, let them take it in at their own pace. And don’t expect a thank-you for the session, like they booked it. That’s enough to start being the adult, even if it isn’t enough yet for them to trust you.

name: t102_pain_p
headline: Human Written
windows: And when the symptoms come and go randomly, the best time to get diagnostics done could be right at the actual time of the crisis, rather than waiting until you feel well enough to make an appointment, and they may be able to treat it while it’s happening. But what if the attacks come almost every day?
You can’t move into the ER.
And normal test results don’t prove the pain is imaginary, just as a treatment that helps doesn’t explain what’s causing it.

name: t102_untangle_p
headline: AI Generated
windows: Differentiation is slow, and it goes on your whole life. If a family, group or relationship won’t let you do this while you’re still part of it, temporary distance may be necessary. Even when it isn’t, a break can let the old programming quiet down long enough for what you actually want to come up. Some people come back later on different terms. Sometimes the leaving turns out to be permanent, because going back would mean disappearing again. You don’t have to know yet which one yours is. As you differentiate, you learn to tell the difference.

name: t102_sharing_p
headline: Human Written
windows: So I’d ask them, before handing over any tricky specifics: “What does the law require you to report?” That’s a normal and expected question. Although personally I wouldn’t even bother with that, because whatever they tell you today, the law can change tomorrow. I’d assume that what you tell won’t be completely confidential, especially if it sounds like something dangerous. You can always rephrase things as a dream narrative to get the emotional content across without triggering alarm bells (although I actually got in trouble with TalkSpace therapy bot even for a dream!). Just don’t hold back a danger that’s happening now from people who can help, and get anyone in danger safe before worrying about the rest. Sometimes telling on yourself is the thing that keeps someone safe, whatever it costs you legally.
